author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Canonical record for Gather Yourselves Together, PKD's novel, preserving a single archive manifestation.
page_summary:
Gather Yourselves Together is the canonical works record for PKD's novel. It preserves a single archive manifestation and gives the work a stable bibliographic home. The preserved item here is Gather Yourselves Together (1994).

Researchers can use this entry to trace publication context, later commentary, and relationships to other works.

structure.form: mainstream literary novel set almost entirely within a single isolated compound during its final days before a political handover

characters.name: Carl Fitter
characters.note: An older American employee of the compound whose relationship with the much younger Barbara Mahler forms the novel's central interpersonal tension during the compound's final days.

characters.name: Verne Tildon
characters.note: A younger American colleague whose presence completes the compound's isolated trio during the handover period.

characters.name: Barbara Mahler
characters.note: A young woman whose relationship with the older Carl Fitter, developed in the compound's final isolated days, is treated by the novel with unusual directness for Dick's early fiction.

settings.name: An American industrial compound in China
settings.note: Set during the final days before the Chinese Communist government's takeover at the close of the civil war period, its emptying-out of ordinary institutional life and purpose functions as the novel's central pressure chamber for its characters' interior lives.

motifs: A liminal, about-to-be-abandoned institutional space as a pressure chamber that surfaces suppressed interpersonal tension once ordinary routine dissolves
Political upheaval kept largely offstage in favor of close, intimate focus on a small isolated cast
A generationally uneven relationship treated with unusual directness rather than moralized or softened
Dispersal and uncertainty rather than resolution as the novel's closing note
reading.significance: Gather Yourselves Together is one of Dick's earliest surviving novel manuscripts, written in the early 1950s during his sustained but ultimately unsuccessful effort to break into mainstream literary fiction before turning primarily to genre science fiction for his living. Unpublished until 1994, over a decade after his death, it offers scholars a rare view of Dick's prose and thematic concerns before his voice had been shaped by pulp science fiction markets, and its focus on a small cast under interpersonal pressure in an isolated, dissolving institutional setting anticipates the character-driven, claustrophobic domestic dramas of his later mainstream novels like Confessions of a Crap Artist.
reading.closing_note: The novel's refusal to resolve either the political handover or its characters' personal entanglements into a clean ending reflects an early instance of Dick's recurring preference for unresolved, open-ended conclusions over tidy narrative closure.

reading_provenance.note: Close reading of the primary text plus attributed evidence from the archive. Candidate: not yet promoted to canonical.
